United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: UNESCO supports Member States in advancing Open Solutions and digital public goods, including Open Access, Open Data, and Free and Open Source Software, through policy support, capacity development, and cooperation. The initiative promotes open, interoperable, and trustworthy information ecosystems that strengthen access to knowledge, transparency, and public participation.

description.narrative:
Rationale Digital public goods and Open Solutions are increasingly recognized as essential enablers of sustainable development, inclusive digital cooperation, and equitable access to information. Open solutions—including Open Access, Open Data, Free and Open Source Software, and related public-interest digital resources—help strengthen transparency, accountability, public participation, and knowledge sharing. However, persistent challenges such as unequal access to digital infrastructure, limited institutional capacities, fragmented policy environments, and barriers to participation continue to restrict the benefits for many communities. UNESCO is uniquely positioned to address these challenges by supporting Member States in developing policies and capacity building that promote open, interoperable, and trustworthy digital public goods. By advancing Open Solutions, the initiative contributes to more inclusive, accessible, and sustainable information ecosystems that support access to knowledge, innovation, and public-interest outcomes.
Implementation Strategy UNESCO will implement the initiative through policy support, technical assistance, capacity development, and multistakeholder cooperation to advance Open Solutions and digital public goods. The programme will provide guidance to Member States on developing and strengthening Open Access and Open Data policies that enhance transparency, accountability, interoperability, and public participation. Capacity-building activities will support institutions and stakeholders strengthening data stewardship practices, and developing the skills needed to manage and sustain open digital ecosystems, with a focus for learning and research. These activiites will promote frameworks for digital public goods, facilitate knowledge exchange, and support the development of interoperable and publicly accessible digital infrastructures. UNESCO will also convene governments, technical communities, civil society, and development partners to foster cooperation, share good practices, and strengthen the role of Open Solutions in advancing inclusive and sustainable development.
